correctness.rationale: Strict matrix-unit multiplication is associative; a nonzero j-fold product is precisely a composable strict chain of j+1 vertices. Thus the nilpotency index at height h>=2 is h. At heights 0 and 1 the full powerset semiring is the two-element distributive lattice, with setwise product as meet. At height 2 the universal unary relation imposes no constraint, and at height 3 the nonzero-product digraph is homomorphically equivalent to a single arc since no vertex can be both source and target; the directed two-edge path (whose images need not be distinct in an input) is a finite obstruction. At h>=4 a four-point chain supplies the directed walk of length two. For each frozen alternating odd cycle, tracking the endpoint equalities v_i=u_j along the arcs yields v_0=u_1=v_2=...=v_{2m}=u_0, so the strict interval at vertex 0 is impossible. Every proper induced substructure splits into paths. If the unique two-walk survives, pin its values to 0,1,2 on the chain walk and extend alternately by 0,1 on the entering tail and 1,2 on the exiting tail; other components map to a single edge. A finite obstruction list would force a bound on the size of the induced support of an obstruction image, contradicting these unbounded minimal induced examples. Wang–Yin–Wang Theorem 1.1 applies in the stated full constant-free signature. For the precise encoding of the displayed absorption identity use empty R1 on the obstruction, rather than universal R1: this leaves all maps unchanged since R1 on the target is universal and gives exactly the binary sum. Direct evaluation proves validity (an empty variable kills the long word; otherwise it is {0} and some binary term must contain 0). Theorem 4.1 and its explicit post-theorem consequence establish precisely the nonderivability asserted at ℓ>(h−1)(k+2).
residual_risks: The recorded 5231-poset enumeration and cycles through length 17 are finite corroboration only; the proof of the unbounded threshold is relational.

evidence: The October 26 target excludes the odd cycle by two-colorability. On a five-point chain, write ij for (i,j): 01→12→23→34 and 01→13→34 give two paths whose union is an undirected 5-cycle. The older argument's hypothesis therefore fails in the interval family. The general finite-basis theorem is a reduction, and Example 4.5 warns that nonfinite basability cannot simply be passed up from a small subalgebra or quotient.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new endpoint-equality contradiction forbids the particular orientation even in nonbipartite targets, while its proper induced substructures still map using only a four-point chain. This is what is needed for every height, not a direct special case of the prior index-three/bipartite theorem.

originality.rationale: The supported increment is the all-finite-poset upper-height obstruction and exact height threshold, not the general duality criterion, the low-index positive case, or invention of the odd-cycle family. The strongest earlier indexed result uses the same oriented odd cycles but its negative theorem assumes index three and a bipartite product graph. The frozen obstruction argument is genuinely stronger for strict intervals, for which product graphs at height at least five need not be bipartite and higher nonzero-product relations are present.
residual_risks: The previously used odd-cycle construction is not novel; only its strict-endpoint obstruction across the full family is credited. A different prior derivation may exist outside the inspected corpus.

value.rationale: This is a natural uniform height threshold for a poset construction that is insensitive to width and branching yet sharply contrasts with flat addition on the same chain multiplication. The obstruction remains informative for nonbipartite high-index targets and gives explicit arbitrarily large minimal induced counterinstances and valid identities with unbounded variable complexity. A bounded small-semigroup census would not supply these conclusions.
residual_risks: The result concerns full powerset algebras of strict intervals, not nonempty powersets, loop-inclusive intervals or arbitrary nilpotent semigroups.
